purpose: The full, browsable listing of a page such as the Careers jobs list: a headline over a toolbar (a search field, one select per facet and one for the order) and every row under its group, as a table from the small breakpoint up and as a list of items below it, with an empty state when nothing matches. A row may carry its client's mark, drawn before the name on the table and above it on phones; a pointer click anywhere on a table row follows the row link; the other columns are metadata in the small overline, each cut to one line with its full text as a tooltip; group headings stick under the site header while their rows scroll. Below the large breakpoint the toolbar folds to the search field and a filter button that reveals the selects, with each applied facet listed under it as a removable chip. A select with more than seven options gains an option search. Search, facets and order are local state over the rows the page carries; a facet is seeded from `?<key>=` in the URL when the value is one the page offers. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'listing-browser', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below, and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box`, `input`, `select`, `table`, `item`, `chip`, `empty-state` and `button` rather than owning any anatomy of its own.
useWhen: Use ListingBrowser for a filterable list of non-article rows (jobs): a listing a reader narrows by text and by a few facets, such as open positions grouped by department.
When every row links to its own page and the listing fits in the page JSON.
avoidWhen: For a short, unfiltered preview of the same rows → use `listing-table`.
For a data table with sorting, selection and pagination inside the product → use `table`.
For a grid of linked topic cards → use `subject-library`.
For the full filterable list of articles or resources → use `article-index`.
For a card grid of customer stories with search and facets → use `story-library`.
related: table` — the composed rows and cells the listing renders from the small breakpoint up.
item` — the list rows the listing renders below the small breakpoint.
empty-state` — the state shown when the search and facets match nothing.
bestPractices: Name the first column after what the row is (`Role`); it is the row's link, and the second column describes the row on phones.
Give every row the facet values it carries under the facet's `key`, so the selects narrow it.
Keep `groups` in the order the reader scans; rows of a group not listed there are not shown.
Make the first entry of `sorts` the order the page is authored in, with an empty `by`.
